subject: GreenLeaf SLA: proposed redundancy / failover amendment and MAP
raw_messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@greenleaf.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: GreenLeaf Procurement <procurement@greenleaf.com>, Kunal Mehta <kunal@greenleaf.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA amendment: multi-region failover / RTO & RPO

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for running the POC last quarter — the latency profiles looked good. Procurement has flagged a requirement for our platform contract: GreenLeaf requires an explicit SLA carve-out covering multi-region failover for our payment-critical workloads.

Specifically we need: 
- RTO <= 30 minutes for cross-region failover (us-west <-> us-east) for production traffic.
- RPO <= 5 minutes for transaction metadata (we retain a small write-ahead cache).
- Monthly failover test window and evidence (logs, timeline) to be retained for 12 months.

Can Redwood commit to this as an addendum? If there is a pricing uplift or recommended config (dedicated capacity, hot-standby region), please send a proposal and any required runbook snippets we should review.

Asha
Head of CloudOps
GreenLeaf Finance

Attachments: none

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@greenleaf.com>
Cc: GreenLeaf Procurement <procurement@greenleaf.com>, Kunal Mehta <kunal@greenleaf.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 09:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment: multi-region failover / RTO & RPO

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear request. We can scope this but will need to align on the implementation model (active-active vs warm-standby), quantize the availability guarantees, and confirm what "transaction metadata" maps to in your topology.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
1) Internal feasibility check with engineering and security.
2) Draft an amendment that ties commitments to the deployment mode (e.g., Dedicated Premium with reserved capacity + cross-region warm caches).
3) Create a mutual action plan (MAP) including runbook excerpts and the monthly test schedule.

I’ll loop in our infra and security leads and follow up with a concrete proposal by EOD Monday (1/12). Would GreenLeaf be okay with a Dedicated Premium configuration for the SLA? That’s typically how we guarantee sub-hour cross-region RTO.

—Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: FW: GreenLeaf SLA request - need feasibility + cost estimate

Neha / Vivek — forwarding GreenLeaf's ask (see below). Key constraints: RTO <= 30m, RPO <= 5m, monthly test evidence retention = 12 months. Procurement wants this codified in an addendum.

Questions for you: 
- Feasibility: can our Dedicated Premium with hot-standby region guarantee 30m RTO and 5m RPO for transactional workloads? Outline assumptions (state replication method, KV cache prewarming, DNS TTLs, load balancer failover timings).
- Failure modes: what are the main risks that would push us beyond 30m? (e.g., cold KV cache rebuild, model weights load times, long tail hardware attach on cloud provider).
- Cost uplift: ballpark OPEX increase (percent) for maintaining hot-standby capacity and monthly test windows with a documented timeline.

Initial notes from me: we should offer two tiers in the proposal: 
A) Warm-standby (reduced-cost): reserved minimal capacity in secondary region, automated cache prewarm on failover — target RTO ~30–45m depending on cache size.
B) Hot-standby (premium): mirror production capacity in secondary region (active-passive), near instant traffic cutover plus continuous DR exercises — target RTO <=30m, RPO <=5m, higher uplift.

Please reply with feasibility and rough numbers by Monday morning so I can synthesize a MAP and pricing for GreenLeaf.

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@greenleaf.com>, GreenLeaf Procurement <procurement@greenleaf.com>, Kunal Mehta <kunal@greenleaf.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: SLA amendment: multi-region failover / RTO & RPO — proposed amendment & MAP

Hi Asha / team — thanks for your patience. Per our internal review (cc: Neha, Vivek, Marissa), please find below Redwood's proposed amendment and a concise mutual action plan. We attach a draft SOW and a runbook excerpt for your review.

Proposal summary (high-level):
- Commitment: For GreenLeaf Finance production workloads on Redwood Dedicated Premium (reserved capacity + hot-standby region), Redwood will target:
  • RTO (cross-region failover): 30 minutes for customer-triggered or automatic failover events, measured from failover start to steady-state traffic in the secondary region.
  • RPO (transaction metadata): <= 5 minutes when using our transactional replication configuration (see runbook).
- Coverage: Commitment applies only to workloads deployed on Dedicated Premium and with the agreed replication configuration enabled. Standard hosted tiers are excluded.
- Evidence & testing: Monthly failover window; Redwood will provide a test report (timeline, event logs, traffic graphs) within 48 hours of the test and will retain reports for 12 months.
- Exclusions / caveats: Third-party network outages beyond our control, active data corruption, or customer-side misconfiguration (DNS mis-entries, incorrect health probes) are excluded. Any reduction in RTO/RPO due to these should be documented with root cause analysis.

Estimated uplift: Hot-standby (Dedicated Premium) + continuous readiness: ~+85% on baseline Dedicated rate (ballpark). Warm-standby option (reserved minimal capacity + automated prewarm) reduces uplift to ~+35% but RTO may be 30–60 minutes depending on cache warm-up. We can provide exact pricing in the SOW (attached).

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
1) Agreement: Redwood to issue an amendment draft (attached SOW) that codifies RTO/RPO targets and test cadence.
2) Onboarding: GreenLeaf to confirm target production clusters and replication configuration.
3) Dry-run: Schedule first monthly test in 30 days; Redwood will run test and deliver report within 48 hours.
4) Ops runbook: Redwood provides runbook snippets (attached) for failover steps, cache prewarm commands, and log collection.
5) Sign-off: After two successful monthly tests, both parties will sign the SLA addendum.

Next steps: Please confirm whether you want the Hot-standby (recommended for payment-critical workloads) or Warm-standby. Once you confirm, we’ll send a priced SOW and DocuSign link for the amendment.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk the MAP.

—Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(t) +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: sow-greenleaf-sla-draft.pdf (Draft SOW), runbook-kv-cache-architecture.png (runbook diagram)
